message.name: SYS_ICD_GCS_FLCC_OBJECT_AVOIDANCE_CMD
message.field: 0: Normal, 1: OA Level1, 2: OA Level2[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:2]

message.name: SYS_ICD_GCS_FLCC_SAR_CTRL
message.description: SAR observation control from GCS to FLCC. One initial request and at most one GCS retry; repeated commands must not toggle observation.
message.field: Observation control: 0 Prepare, 1 Start, 2 Stop. Values 3 through 255 are undefined.
Observation mode selection. All values from 0 through 255 are allowed; detailed mapping is TBD.

message.name: SYS_ICD_FLCC_GCS_PMU_STATUS
message.field: Fuel_Quantity[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:100]. ECU: an estimate derived from RPM/load and the ECU's configured tank/fuel inventory, not a fuel sensor reading. 100 DOES NOT BY ITSELF MEAN A FULL TANK: while TM60 Initial_Fail bit 0x20 is set the ECU holds no valid fuel quantity and substitutes a full tank, so this field reads 100 as a placeholder. Qualify it with that bit - with 0x20 set display it as not initialised, never as a confirmed full tank; with 0x20 clear a reading of 100 is an ordinary estimate. Legacy PMU: unchanged, no placeholder behaviour.

message.name: SYS_ICD_FLCC_GCS_OBJECT_AVOIDANCE_STATUS
message.field: 0: Normal, 1: OA Level1, 2: OA Level2[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:2]
Bit0~Bit7 to Sectors 0~7, 0:none, 1:object exists[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]

message.name: SYS_ICD_FLCC_GCS_SAR_STATUS
message.description: SAR device status from FLCC to GCS, sent periodically at 5 Hz.
message.field: SAR observation status: 0 Disconnected, 1 Ready, 2 Stopped, 3 Started, 4 SAR Not Responding after the FC 2-second response window.

FC-maintained valid SAR Heart_Beat reception count. Increment by one per valid CAN 0x510, not per TM transmission. Reset on FC boot during the common single-battery power reset; no persistence or separate SAR reboot detection. No terminal-count handling required in the operating lifetime.

message.name: SYS_ICD_GCS_FLCC_ECU_ENERGY_CFG
message.description: TC60 (ECU). Energy configuration from GCS to FLCC, operator action only. The FC sends one ENERGYCFG frame per accepted command and retries the identical frame to a maximum of three transmissions; the result appears in TM61 Cfg_Result and Cfg_Attempts.
message.field: Tank capacity[SF:0.01, MIN:10, MAX:10000]. Raw UINT16, 0.01 L per count, so raw 800 is 8.00 L. Operator enters litres from 0.10 to 100.00; KGCS sends round(litres * 100). THE PHYSICAL SIZE OF THE TANK, not how much is in it. Send 65535 to keep the ECU's current capacity. Verified exactly against TM61 Tank.

Current total fuel in tank[SF:0.01, MIN:0, MAX:Tank]. Raw UINT16, 0.01 L per count. Operator reads the tank level indication and enters the ABSOLUTE total now in the tank, 0.00 L up to the tank capacity; KGCS sends round(litres * 100). NEVER an amount added, and never computed by adding a refuelling quantity to a previous reading. May not exceed the tank capacity being set, or the ECU's retained capacity if none is being set. Send 65535 to keep the ECU's current quantity. The ECU stores this across power cycles and decrements it as fuel is burned. Verified only indirectly, through an integer fuel percentage - see the TC60 comment above.

Battery capacity[SF:0.1, MIN:50, MAX:1000]. Raw UINT16, 0.1 Ah per count, so raw 220 is 22.0 Ah. Operator enters 5.0 to 100.0 Ah; KGCS sends round(Ah * 10). Send 65535 to keep the ECU's current capacity. Verified exactly against TM61 Battery.

Optional state-of-charge correction[SF:0.1, MIN:0, MAX:1000]. Raw UINT16, 0.1 percent per count, so raw 850 is 85.0 percent. Operator enters 0.0 to 100.0 percent; KGCS sends round(percent * 10). OPTIONAL: the ECU estimates state of charge from battery voltage at power-up, and this field exists only to correct that estimate deliberately. The normal value is 65535, keep current. Verified against TM61 Battery_SOC within 0.1 percentage point.

message.name: SYS_ICD_FLCC_GCS_ECU_MODE_STATUS
message.description: TM60 (ECU). ECU operating modes, RPM target and start permission, as received. 10 Hz. Informational only: the ECU enforces its own modes and start permissions.
message.field: Governor RPM target[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Raw UINT16, 1 rpm per count. Display as a number. ZERO MEANS THE ECU IS NOT GOVERNING RPM - engine stopped, cranking, MANUAL, or certain fail and stop modes - AND IS NOT PROOF OF AN ENGINE STOP. A missing tachometer pulse can also leave it non-zero; once the ECU enters FAIL_TACHO it reports zero.

Age of the MODESTS reading[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Milliseconds since the last MODESTS reply, saturating at 65535, and reported as 65535 while Data_Valid bit 0 is clear. In normal operation it settles around 80 ms, which is the gap between the ECU poll and this message; that is not a fault.

ECU system state[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:15]. Raw 4-bit value. Values: 1 INITIALIZATION; 2 READY; 3 ENGINE_RUN; 4 USER_SHELL. ALL OTHER VALUES INCLUDING 0 ARE UNDEFINED - display the raw number as Unknown and give it no meaning.

ECU operation mode[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:15]. Raw 4-bit value. Values: 1 DO_NOTHING; 3 STANDBY; 4 STARTUP; 5 RUNNING; 6 STOP. VALUES 0 AND 2 ARE UNDEFINED, as is anything above 6 - display the raw number as Unknown. This is the field KGCS uses to enable the TC60 Apply button: the ECU accepts an energy configuration only in 1 DO_NOTHING or 3 STANDBY, and leaving those two modes cancels a transaction in progress.

ECU control mode[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Values: 1 NONE; 2 MANUAL; 3 STARTUP; 4 STOP; 5 FIXED_RPM; 6 EMS; 7 INACTIVE; 8 FAIL_TACHO; 9 FAIL_CURR_SENSOR; 10 FAIL_VOLT_SENSOR. All other values including 0 are undefined - display the raw number as Unknown. The three FAIL_ modes are ECU-detected sensor faults and warrant operator attention.

ECU alert level[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Values: 0 NONE; 1 ADVISORY, meaning plan to land; 2 IMMEDIATE, meaning land now. All other values are undefined - display the raw number as Unknown. The ECU raises ADVISORY for a low state of charge, EMS THERMAL_HOLD or FORCED_CHARGE, or low fuel or fuel endurance, and clears it two seconds after all causes clear. It raises IMMEDIATE for a battery at landing reserve, or a low state of charge together with low fuel or a cylinder head above 260 degC, and clears to the then-current level five seconds after the causes clear.

ECU energy-management state[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Values: 0 INIT; 1 START; 2 WARMUP; 3 CHARGE; 4 IDLE; 5 DISCHARGE; 6 EMERGENCY; 7 STOPPING; 8 THERMAL_HOLD; 9 FORCED_CHARGE. All other values are undefined - display the raw number as Unknown. EMERGENCY, THERMAL_HOLD and FORCED_CHARGE are the states that also drive Alert_Level.

Result of the last engine start attempt[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Values: 0 OK, start gates passed - BUT ALSO MEANS NO ATTEMPT SINCE POWER-ON, so it is not proof of a running engine; 4 BLOCKED_ALREADY_RUNNING; 5 BLOCKED_EEPROM_BAD; 6 BLOCKED_CALIB_MISSING; 7 BLOCKED_TACHO_FAULT; 8 BLOCKED_THROTTLE_UNCALIBRATED; 9 BLOCKED_CHOKE_UNCALIBRATED; 10 BLOCKED_STARTER_UNCALIBRATED; 11 BLOCKED_SHELL_ACTIVE; 12 BLOCKED_NOT_STANDBY; 13 BLOCKED_FUEL_LEVEL; 15 ABORTED_TIMEOUT, cranked but did not run in time; 16 ABORTED_NO_ROTATION, starter driven but no tachometer pulses; 17 ABORTED_STOPPED_AT_HANDOVER; 18 ABORTED_STOP_REQUESTED; 19 BLOCKED_CURRENT_FAULT, the load current or battery current reading is bad - start works again once both readings are good. CODES 1, 2, 3 AND 14 ARE UNDEFINED, as is anything above 19 - display the raw number as Unknown. A BLOCKED_ code is a start refused before cranking; an ABORTED_ code is a start terminated after cranking began. The code persists until the next start attempt.

ECU boot and calibration prerequisites, bitmask[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Bits: 0x01 HEADER_BAD, stored-configuration header invalid; 0x02 EEPROM_LAYOUT, stored-configuration layout invalid; 0x04 CALIB_MISSING, a sensor calibration is missing; 0x20 FUEL_LEVEL, no good fuel quantity is saved in the ECU - it was never set, cannot be read, is below zero, or exceeds the tank. Clear it by sending TC60 with a Fuel value. WHILE THIS BIT IS SET THE ECU SUBSTITUTES A FULL TANK, so TM1 Fuel_Quantity reads 100 percent and that 100 percent is not a real measurement - display it as unset, not as full. BITS 0x08, 0x10, 0x40 AND 0x80 ARE UNDEFINED - show them as set-but-unknown and give them no meaning. EVERY DEFINED BIT BLOCKS ENGINE START INSIDE THE ECU, which performs that check itself, so a non-zero value needs operator attention; KGCS displays it, raw value included, and MUST NOT evaluate it or build a start interlock on it.

Reception and freshness flags[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Bit0 at least one MODESTS has been decoded since boot; Bit1 the last one arrived no more than 500 ms ago. Other bits are reserved and zero. While Bit1 is clear the other fields hold their last decoded values and must be displayed as a greyed-out last-known reading with Mode_Age, never as current ECU state. While Bit0 is clear no reading exists at all and every field reads zero with Mode_Age 65535.

message.name: SYS_ICD_FLCC_GCS_ECU_ENERGY_STATUS
message.description: TM61 (ECU). ECU energy configuration and endurance, as received, plus the ENERGYCFG transaction result. 1 Hz.
message.field: Configured tank capacity as reported by the ECU[SF:0.01, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Raw UINT16, 0.01 L per count, so raw 800 is 8.00 L. READ-ONLY STATUS, not an input field; it is changed through TC60 Tank and is the exact read-back the FC verifies that command against.

Configured battery capacity as reported by the ECU[SF:0.1, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Raw UINT16, 0.1 Ah per count, so raw 220 is 22.0 Ah. READ-ONLY STATUS, not an input field; it is changed through TC60 Battery and is the exact read-back the FC verifies that command against.

Estimated remaining fuel endurance[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Raw UINT16, 1 second per count, with TWO SPECIAL VALUES THAT OVERRIDE THE SCALE: 65534 means 65534 seconds or more, display as "65534 s or more" and never as an exact time; 65535 means Unknown, display as "Unknown" and NEVER as zero or as "0 s". Any other value is a count of seconds. The ECU reports 65535 whenever no fuel is being burned, so a stopped engine normally shows Unknown - that is correct, not a fault. The FC does not compute or estimate this value and KGCS must not either.

Age of the energy reading[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:65535]. Milliseconds since the last energy status reply, saturating at 65535, and reported as 65535 while Data_Valid bit 0 is clear. NORMALLY ABOUT 970 ms ON A HEALTHY LINK, because the ECU is polled once a second and this message is sent on a different phase of that second. Do not treat that as a communication error; judge staleness from Data_Valid bit 1.

Battery state of charge[SF:0.1, MIN:-32768, MAX:32767]. Signed INT16, 0.1 percent per count, so raw 850 is 85.0 percent. VALID ONLY WHILE Data_Valid BIT 2 IS SET. Unlike every other field in this message it is NOT held when it goes stale: the FC transmits zero, so a cleared bit 2 must be displayed as Unknown and never as 0.0 percent. This is the value the FC verifies a TC60 SOC correction against, within 0.1 percentage point.

Reception and freshness flags[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Bit0 at least one energy status reply has been decoded since boot; Bit1 the last one arrived no more than 2500 ms ago; Bit2 the battery state of charge is available and arrived no more than 500 ms ago. Other bits are reserved and zero. While Bit1 is clear, Tank, Battery and Endurance hold their last decoded values and must be shown as a stale last-known reading with Energy_Age - the numbers not changing is what a dead link looks like.

Outcome of the last ENERGYCFG transaction[SF:N/A, MIN:0, MAX:255]. Values: 0 NONE, nothing sent since boot; 1 IN_PROGRESS, ongoing; 2 OK, verified by FC read-back; 3 MISMATCH_AFTER_3, three frames sent and never verified; 4 CANCELLED_MODE_CHANGE, the ECU left standby mid-transaction; 5 REJECTED_RANGE, a value was out of range and nothing was sent; 6 REJECTED_MODE, the ECU was not in standby and nothing was sent; 7 REJECTED_NOT_ECU, no confirmed ECU 2.00 or higher and nothing was sent; 8 TX_FAIL, a frame could not be handed to the CAN interface. LATCHED - it describes the last transaction and is retransmitted unchanged at 1 Hz, so act on a change of value and not on each reception. OK MEANS THE FC'S READ-BACK COMPARISON SUCCEEDED - not that the ECU acknowledged or accepted anything, since the protocol defines no acknowledgment and there is no rollback. Where Fuel equalled Tank the comparison cannot distinguish acceptance from a placeholder; see TC60. See the TM61 comment above for the full per-code handling.

ENERGYCFG frames actually handed to the bus in that transaction[SF:1, MIN:0, MAX:3]. A PROGRESS COUNT, NOT A FAILURE COUNT - while Cfg_Result is 1 IN_PROGRESS display it as "attempt N of 3". It is 0 for any result that was refused before transmission, and 1 for a command verified on the first frame.
